**(d) The declared two-body Coulomb model.** As a further model assumption,
take two **distinguishable** spinless massive particles with declared mass
parameters $m_{1},m_{2}>0$ (unit kg) and opposite declared charges: particle 1
carries charge $-q_{-}$ and particle 2 carries charge $+q_{+}$, where the
charge magnitudes $q_{-},q_{+}>0$ are read in coulombs. Declare the **pair
coupling**
$$\kappa:=\frac{q_{-}q_{+}}{4\pi\varepsilon_{0}},\qquad \varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1},$$
where $\mu_{0}$ is the declared magnetic constant of the SI conventions and
$c$ the speed of light, both as in clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the identification
$\kappa=q_{-}q_{+}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$ is a constitutive assumption of the
model, and $\kappa$ is read in $\mathrm{J\,m}$. Its equal-magnitude,
net-neutral submodel is $q_{-}=q_{+}=q>0$, with charges $-q,+q$ and
$\kappa=q^{2}/(4\pi\varepsilon_{0})$; this is the branch used by the later
relative-dipole consumers. The two-particle state space is the Hilbert tensor product of
two copies of the one-particle space of clause (a) as in
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], identified with
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C)$ through
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]; the spin-zero internal
factor is trivial, and because the two particles are of different species no
symmetrisation is imposed (the case of identical species belongs to the
identical-particle sector of P6 and is not used here). The **assigned energy
operator** is
$$H_{2}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{1}}\Delta_{x_{1}}-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m_{2}}\Delta_{x_{2}}-\frac{\kappa}{|x_{1}-x_{2}|},\qquad D(H_{2}):=H^{2}(\mathbb R^{6};\mathbb C),$$
which is self-adjoint by clause (c) of
[[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]]. Let
$$\Phi(x_{1},x_{2}):=(R,r),\qquad R:=\frac{m_{1}x_{1}+m_{2}x_{2}}{M},\quad r:=x_{1}-x_{2},\quad M:=m_{1}+m_{2},$$
be the centre-of-mass/relative coordinate map of that theorem, with its
unitary $U_{\Phi}$. The model declares the **centre-of-mass/relative reading**
$U_{\Phi}H_{2}U_{\Phi}^{-1}=T_{R}\otimes I+I\otimes C_{\mu}$ of clause (c) of
that theorem, with the **reduced mass**
$$\mu:=\frac{m_{1}m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\qquad(\text{unit }\mathrm{kg}),$$
the centre-of-mass kinetic operator $T_{R}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2M}\Delta_{R}$
and the **relative operator** $C_{\mu}:=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2\mu}\Delta_{r}-\frac{\kappa}{|r|}$;
the relative operator is exactly the one-centre Coulomb operator of clause
(b) with mass parameter $\mu$. The energy operators $H_{2}$, $T_{R}$ and
$C_{\mu}$ are each read in joules. The model further declares the **fixed-nucleus
reading**: the one-centre model of clauses (b), (c) with mass parameter $m_{1}$
is read as the limiting description in which the second particle is
infinitely heavy, $\mu\to m_{1}$ as $m_{2}\to\infty$ at fixed $m_{1},\kappa$;
this is a declared limiting reading, and no convergence theorem for operators
or states is asserted by it.

relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the coordinate

energy** is the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix
$$H_{a}:=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W},$$

data: they are not derived from the Coulomb model and they replace the
unbounded operators $H_{\kappa},D_{j}$ by their compressions throughout this

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m_1,m_2,\mu,M,\kappa,\hbar$
be as in [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]], let $C_\mu$ and $T_R$ be
the relative and centre-of-mass kinetic operators there, let
$u_1\in L^2(\mathbb R^3_r)$ be any nonzero relative ground vector with
$C_\mu u_1=E_1u_1$, where $E_1=-\frac{\mu\kappa^2}{2\hbar^2}$, and let
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3_R;\mathbb C)$ be a nonzero centre-of-mass
test function. Consider the product vector
$$\Psi:=\varphi\otimes u_1\in L^2(\mathbb R^3_R)\widehat\otimes L^2(\mathbb R^3_r),$$
viewed as an element of $L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ through the identification of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]. This example verifies
that:

(c) the relative bound state $u_1$ is an eigenvector of the relative operator $C_\mu$, but the two-body operator has no eigenvalues at all ([[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]] (d)); the relative bound energy is a threshold of the continuous spectrum of the total operator, so "relative bound state" and "bound state of the two-body problem" are distinct notions.

1.1 [The product vector is not an eigenvector] By [F2], $(T_R\otimes I)\Psi=(T_R\varphi)\otimes u_1$ and $(I\otimes C_\mu)\Psi=\varphi\otimes(C_\mu u_1)=\varphi\otimes E_1u_1=E_1\Psi$ by [F1]; hence $(T_R\otimes I+I\otimes C_\mu)\Psi=E_1\Psi+(T_R\varphi)\otimes u_1$, and the difference from $E_1\Psi$ is $(T_R\varphi)\otimes u_1$. By [F3] $T_R\varphi\ne0$ and $u_1\ne0$, so this difference is nonzero: $\Psi$ is not an eigenvector at $E_1$. The full no-eigenvalue result [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]] (d) also rules out every other energy, so $\Psi$ is not an eigenvector at any energy. This is (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Energy strictly above the threshold] Taking pairings with $\Psi$ and using [F2] and [F1], $\langle(T_R\otimes I+I\otimes C_\mu)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\|u_1\|^2\langle T_R\varphi,\varphi\rangle+\|u_1\|^2E_1\|\varphi\|^2=\|u_1\|^2(E_1\|\varphi\|^2+\langle T_R\varphi,\varphi\rangle)$, and $\langle T_R\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\frac{4\pi^2\hbar^2}{2M}\int|\xi|^2|\widehat\varphi(\xi)|^2d\xi>0$ by [F3] applied to the nonzero function $\varphi$ (the integrand is nonnegative and not a.e. zero). Hence the energy of $\Psi$ is strictly larger than $E_1\|\Psi\|^2$, and since $\|\Psi\|^2=\|\varphi\|^2\|u_1\|^2$, $\Psi/\|\Psi\|$ is a unit vector with energy $E_1+\langle T_R\varphi,\varphi\rangle/\|\varphi\|^2>E_1$, this vector lies strictly above the bottom $E_1$ of the spectrum; by the no-eigenvalue theorem of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]] (d) no nonzero vector at all attains $E_1$. This is (b). [step 1.1, F1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Relative eigenvalue versus total spectrum] The relative vector $u_1$ is an eigenvector of $C_\mu$ at $E_1$ by [F1]; but by the actual no-eigenvalue theorem of [[thm-nrqm-coulomb-two-body-reduced-mass]] (d), no nonzero vector at all satisfies the two-body eigenvalue equation, and $E_1$ is the bottom of the continuous spectrum of the total operator. This is (c). [step 2.1, F1, algebra]

extension
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] (a

factor is a declared finite-dimensional subspace of the two-body Coulomb
relative-coordinate model with compressed dipole matrices and compressed
Coulomb energy, and whose channel dipole coupling $\eta_0\sum_jD_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\otimes\phi(g_j)$
to a finite family of cutoff mode vectors, with declared real Cartesian channel weights, is declared model data. It also
adopts the prescribed dipole-drive model
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-dipole-drive-and-long-wavelength]] with its
long-wavelength regime, and the vacuum-preparation and quantized-field
assumption
[[post-nrqm-light-matter-vacuum-preparation-and-emission-assumption]]. The
identification of a laboratory system, field or apparatus with any of these
models is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]).

**What the page proves conditionally.**
[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] is the page's
mathematics: the explicit factorisation of the single-vertex emission
kernel, the normalised photon-energy law, its concentration at the transition
energy for a continuous positive mode density, and the strict positivity of
the law on windows of positive density.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-emission-and-absorption-coefficients]]
proves the single-vertex emission and absorption amplitudes of the model, the
exact-model control of the one-photon level-$b$ projection probability by the
explicit Dyson tail, and the exact mirror relation between emission into and
absorption from a unit one-photon vector.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] proves the
limit of the single-vertex coefficient per unit time and declares the model
rate coefficient $\Gamma_{b}=2\pi\eta_{0}^{2}J_{b}(\Delta)/\hbar$ under a
continuous positive mode density, with the above-cutoff case tending to zero.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-stimulated-dipole-drive-transitions]] proves the
first-order amplitudes of the prescribed classical drive, the equal
stimulated emission and absorption coefficients for the same physical gap and prescribed real field, and
the exact identification of declared two-level Pauli data with the circular
and linear two-level drive models of the driven-dynamics page.
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-dipole-selection-rules]] proves the necessary
angular and parity conditions on the uncompressed dipole matrix elements, and
transfers their vanishing to compressed matrices when the declared finite-level
subspace is spanned by a finite subfamily of bound states and its declared
orthonormal basis is chosen from that same subfamily. All of these are
conditional consequences of the cited postulates, mathematics and model data;
their units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**What the page does not claim.** The page derives no Maxwell equation, no
mode assignment, no Lorentz transformation law, no massless limit of the
massive model and no coupling constant. It contains no experiment: there is no
apparatus, preparation, calibration, count, frequency, efficiency, background
or uncertainty budget anywhere on the page, and none is invented. It asserts
no measured spectral line, no measured rate, lifetime or linewidth, and no
exponential decay law; the model rate coefficient of
[[pthm-nrqm-light-matter-golden-rule-limit-and-rate-reading]] is a limit of an
explicit model quantity, and its use as a decay constant over a time window
would require additional adopted assumptions, as the sources record
(Binney §9.3.1 on the continuum and long-time approximations; Box 9.2 on
spontaneous emission as a zero-point-field mechanism added to the classical
treatment). The page also does not claim that the coincidence of any model
number with a measured ratio proves the framework, and it reports no
statistical comparison: a comparison with data would test the combined model
and apparatus assumptions, would require a declared sampling and measurement
model, and would carry finite-sample fluctuations and systematic
uncertainties.
